source.title: Understanding the Difficulty of Training Transformers
source.authors: Liyuan Liu; Xiao-Dong Liu; Jian-Feng Gao; Wei-Zhu Chen; Jiawei Han

record.file_problem: The supplied text includes the paper and appendices; no truncation or garbling affecting the relevant findings is apparent.
record.tranche_reason: Tests training stability in deep Transformers, a new architecture and task setting relative to the listed versions, and reports convergence or divergence outcomes.
record.gate_note: The paper reports Transformer convergence and divergence and BLEU scores on translation tasks. It does not report training classification error on CIFAR or the other benchmark outcomes specified by V1–V6. The BLEU results are development/evaluation metrics, not training-error measures.
record.test_reason: Section 5.3 directly tests Fixup without normalization in residual Transformers and reports divergent training, bearing on the Fixup clauses of V3 and V6 in a new setting. The recorded Post-LN, Pre-LN and Admin results do not themselves test the specified versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors attribute instability to residual-branch dependence amplifying parameter changes, rather than gradient vanishing alone, and conclude that Admin improves stability, convergence speed and evaluation performance while allowing stronger residual dependence later in training.
record.recipe_differences: Transformer training on machine translation datasets; compares Post-LN, Pre-LN, and Admin initialization, with BLEU and convergence outcomes rather than CIFAR classification training error.
record.method_sensitivity: Training outcome varies with architecture (Post-LN versus Pre-LN versus Admin), depth, and optimizer hyperparameter settings. Longer warmup alone did not stabilize 18-layer Post-LN training in the reported experiment.

fits_no_version.finding: Post-LN Transformer convergence depends on depth and optimizer settings; Pre-LN and Admin stabilize the reported runs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Normalization placement and residual-branch scaling affect Transformer training stability on translation tasks.

fits_no_version.finding: The 18L–18L Pre-LN and Admin models achieve BLEU 28.38 and 29.03 on WMT’14 En-De.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Admin improves translation evaluation performance over Pre-LN in this setting.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: The study concerns Transformer machine translation, not the classification benchmarks and training-error measures named in the claim versions. Several convergence outcomes are stated in prose without detailed per-run uncertainty; BLEU results do not establish training classification error.
record.rows_left_out: No reported outcomes within the 60-row limit were left out.

untested.parts: Convolutional-network training classification error on CIFAR-10/100, including random or corrupted labels.
Teacher-student ReLU optimization, spurious local minima and extra student neurons.
Plain versus residual batch-normalized CNN training error, longer training, and specially initialized deep plain tanh networks.
Activation-matched initializations in plain networks, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, and very deep plain convolutional trainability.
Learning rates relative to measured stability thresholds, squared loss, curvature reduction and edge-of-stability trajectories.
Batch normalization's effects on accuracy gain and learning-rate tolerance; quantitative training-speed comparisons for Fixup.

missing.what: Fixup without layer normalization produces divergent training in the 18-layer Transformer comparison. Record the half-precision and dropout conditions and the authors' qualified explanation that these could destabilize Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: States for rows linked to none are cannot_determine relative to these claim versions; this does not dispute the reported convergence outcomes. The Fixup finding qualifies transfer to Transformers and does not contradict its original CNN results.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 training classification error, random or corrupted labels, convolutional networks, and the specified optimizer and stopping conditions.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems, spurious minima, and student width relative to teacher width.

Plain batch-normalized convolutional networks versus shortcut versions on ImageNet or CIFAR-10; plain tanh or convolutional networks trained with special initialization; residual networks trained without normalization using Fixup.
Activation-matched, orthogonal, or Gaussian initialization comparisons in plain networks and the specified depth and trainability outcomes.
Learning rates relative to stability limits, squared-loss training, curvature or sharpness, and edge-of-stability behavior.
Batch normalization comparisons on the specified datasets and Fixup comparisons of residual networks with and without normalization.

rows.subject: 18-layer Post-LN Transformer
rows.operation_detail: Trained on WMT’14 En-De; training diverged.
rows.note: The text says the 18-layer Post-LN model diverges and is omitted from the graph.
rows.check: Transformer divergence does not measure any listed version; both compared architectures already contain residual shortcuts.

rows.subject: 18-layer Pre-LN Transformer
rows.operation_detail: Trained on WMT’14 En-De; training converged.
rows.note: The authors describe Pre-LN as converging in all tested settings.
rows.check: Pre-LN Transformer convergence does not test plain-network initialization, batch normalization or the listed shortcut comparisons.

rows.subject: 18-layer Admin (Post-LN) Transformer
rows.operation_detail: Trained with Admin initialization on WMT’14 En-De; training converged.
rows.note: The text says it converges and outperforms 18-layer Pre-LN in the reported comparison.
rows.check: Admin convergence is supported, but this residual Transformer initialization does not test V4's plain-network claim or Fixup.

rows.subject: 12-layer Post-LN Transformer
rows.operation_detail: Trained on WMT’14 En-De; training diverged.
rows.note: Table 2 records the Post-LN result as “failed”; the text states 12-layer Post-LN diverges.
rows.check: The reported divergence is correct but does not measure a listed version.

rows.subject: 12-layer Pre-LN Transformer
rows.operation_detail: Trained on WMT’14 En-De; training converged.
rows.note: The text says Pre-LN converges in all settings.
rows.check: The reported convergence is correct but does not measure a listed version.

rows.subject: 12-layer Admin (Post-LN) Transformer
rows.operation_detail: Trained with Admin initialization on WMT’14 En-De; training converged.
rows.note: Table 2 reports BLEU 28.58; the text describes Admin as stabilizing deeper-model training.
rows.check: Admin convergence does not measure a listed version; BLEU 28.58 is an evaluation result.

rows.subject: 18-layer Post-LN Transformer
rows.operation_detail: Trained on WMT’14 En-Fr; training failed.
rows.note: Table 2 records “failed”; the accompanying text states 18-layer Post-LN diverges.
rows.check: Table 2's failed 18L–18L model is on WMT’14 En-De, not En-Fr. The failed En-Fr model has a 60-layer encoder and 12-layer decoder.

rows.subject: 18-layer Pre-LN Transformer
rows.operation_detail: Trained on WMT’14 En-Fr; BLEU reported.
rows.note: BLEU is a translation evaluation score, not training classification error or a direct convergence measure.
rows.check: BLEU 28.38 belongs to WMT’14 En-De, not En-Fr. It does not measure a listed version.

rows.subject: 18-layer Admin (Post-LN) Transformer
rows.operation_detail: Trained with Admin initialization on WMT’14 En-Fr; BLEU reported.
rows.note: BLEU is a translation evaluation score, not training classification error or a direct convergence measure.
rows.check: BLEU 29.03 belongs to WMT’14 En-De, not En-Fr. It is Admin evaluation performance, not evidence for a listed version.

rows.subject: 18-layer Post-LN Transformer
rows.operation_detail: Tested across a learning-rate and optimizer-hyperparameter grid on IWSLT’14 De-En; reported to diverge in 7 of 15 settings.
rows.note: The paper reports an aggregate across grid settings, not per-setting outcomes in the supplied prose.
rows.check: Figure 10 uses 6-layer encoder/decoder Transformer-small models, not 18-layer models, and removes warmup. The seven failures among 15 settings are correctly reported but do not establish V5's curvature or stability-threshold behavior.

rows.subject: 18-layer Pre-LN Transformer
rows.operation_detail: Tested across a learning-rate and optimizer-hyperparameter grid on IWSLT’14 De-En; reported to converge in all 15 settings.
rows.note: The paper reports an aggregate across grid settings, not per-setting outcomes in the supplied prose.
rows.check: Figure 10 uses 6-layer encoder/decoder Transformer-small models, not 18-layer models, without warmup. Convergence in all 15 settings does not measure a listed version.
